BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to the right to protection; adding a new section tochapter 9.41 RCW; and creating new sections.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature finds that the United Stateswas founded on the principles of freedom from persecution by thegovernment. The federal and state governments were not intended tohave the power they have surmised in the last eighty years. Washingtoncitizens have the right to the protections in section 2 of this act, aswas set out in the United States Constitution. No governmental entityhas the authority to supersede constitutional guarantees.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 9.41 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Any lawful citizen of Washington has the right under the UnitedStates Constitution to protect themselves including, but not limitedto: (a) The use of guns and ammunition; (b) The use of mace or other repellants; and (c) Any other means necessary to stop an assailant. p. 1 SB 6473 (2) Any lawful citizen of Washington has the right to defendhimself or herself, unless he or she is in the act of committing acrime, without interference from federal or state agencies. (3) Law abiding citizens of Washington shall not have their gun orammunition rights waived by any governmental agency nor shall theirguns or ammunition be tracked with markings or radio frequencyidentification dust, paint, or any other direct identifiers. (4) Any lawful citizen of Washington has the constitutional rightto privacy in his or her home including, but not limited to, his or herfarm, vehicle, trailer, or other place of domicile, and to be anonymousas long as he or she is not in the act of committing a crime.
This act may be known and cited as theWashington right to protection act.
